items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We also had a visit of Tommy Dorsey one night... so he played a couple of numbers with us.

ctx.x: One day, the landlord of the house where I had lived with Beezie on 154th street came to see me and told me that he had a room to rent and I jumped at the opportunity quicker than it takes to say'Jack Rabbit', because this fellow and I had many things in common which I had discovered when I lived in his house before Beezie and I separated. His name wa s Earl Norman and his wife's name was Stella. I really felt at home with these people who were more like a brother and sister to me than my landlord and landlady.

Sy Oliver had left the orchestra of Tommy Dorsey for whom he had been the arranger after he had split from Jimmie Lunceford and it must have been around the middle of November, 1946, that I heard through the grapevine that Sy was forming an orchestra and would be auditioning musicians at a rehearsal studio on Broadway.

The audition had not started when I arrived, but there must have been at least 60 musicians in the studio. Sy lived not far from me on St. Nichols Avenue and we had met many times, mostly on the corner of 155th street, and St. Nichols Avenue in front of "Fat Man's Bar".
